communication_expectations: Marcus is 61, good-humoured, deflects embarrassment with jokes; a patient, unhurried style draws him out.
caregiver_rules: Not applicable - the patient speaks for themselves.
patient_goals: Feel like himself at family dinners

assessment_areas.case_context: Rapid exhaustion with short walks and self-care.
Dressing and kitchen tasks slowed by right-hand clumsiness.
Meals have become slow with coughing fits; clothes looser - relevant health-behavior territory.
acceptable_approaches: asking about eating, drinking, mealtimes, weight

assessment_areas.case_context: Family meals matter to him; he has begun withdrawing from them.
Blood-pressure tablet and blood thinner post-stroke.

referral_assessment_context.clinical_summary: Coughing during meals and liquids with a recent choking episode after stroke suggests a possible unassessed swallowing concern; the patient is embarrassed and has begun avoiding family meals; clothes fit more loosely.
scope_considerations: Endurance and daily-activity work is appropriate PT territory.
Swallowing assessment or dietary-texture prescriptions should not be treated as the student's role.
safety_considerations: Coughing/choking with intake after stroke can carry aspiration risk; a recent frightening choking episode raises the priority of timely coordination.
reasonable_care_pathways: The patient's stroke team or primary medical provider
referral_assessment_context.urgency_context: Prompt coordination is generally warranted once the choking episode is disclosed; routine if only mild mealtime coughing surfaced.
acceptable_alternatives: Recommending the stroke team be informed
Framing it as something worth checking before it causes harm, without naming a discipline
not_expected: Swallowing screening maneuvers by the student
Referral action when mealtime symptoms were never disclosed
